title.narrative: Activity under preparation Choose Europe for Science

description.narrative: Contract related to: Choose Europe for Science - The action is structured as follows:Budget Support: EUR 62 MComplementary measures: EUR 24.8 M of which:Twinning grants: EUR 6.5Indirect management to support the availability of quality data for evidence-based policy making: EUR 2.5 MIndirect management to support literacy skills for female manufacturing workers: EUR 1.8 MIndirect management for pilot Global Gateway scholarship scheme and work placement in European companies: EUR 14 MEvaluation and audits: EUR 0.2 MKey interventions areas include: (i) the national policy on scholarships to support access to secondary education, including girls in STEM, (ii) the introduction of dual training modalities[1] in technical high schools and industry placements for higher education students in STEM/applied science degrees in strong linkage with the EU and EU investments, (iii) the ¿low carbon (promoting both climate change mitigation and adaptation) and (iv) digital update of the curriculum and of teachers¿ reforms. The action also strengthens the governance of the education system: it accompanies the Public Financial Management (PFM) reforms in education, improving the quality of financial data, of programme-budgeting and accountability; and it promotes the collection and use of data on climate-change, disability and multilinguism for Human Right-Based Approach (HRBA) policy-making. Gender is mainstreamed all along the intervention logic of the action, including at the level of the overall objective (Gender Marker 2). The action has a strong complementarity with ASEAN programmes promoting people-to-people connectivity in education and skills, notably the Regional Sustainable Connectivity Package as well as the Erasmus+ programme.Budget Support and complementary measures are envisaged. The complementary measures consist of, among other, two Twinnings with EU Member States to enrich the peer-to-peer policy dialogue on skills, applied sciences and STEM in secondary and higher education for the green and digital transformation of agriculture and industrial value chains with a focus on energy and clean water ¿ selected priorities for Cambodia under Global Gateway. Another complementary measure consists of a dedicated scholarship scheme for full-degree studies in STEM and applied sciences in Europe preferably with EU Member States. The scheme will also include the provision of expertise for guidelines on scholarships, students¿ selection and pre-departure/financial support for Cambodian students to study in Europe, foundation years and work placements (work-based learning, internships and graduate careers) in EU companies. This component will strengthen the linkage between Cambodia and Europe in line with the key areas of the EU GG priorities and European investments in Cambodia.The impact of the action is to increase the gender equality in the number of Cambodian youths and adults who have relevant competencies and skills, responding to the medium- and long- term needs of a low-carbon and digitalised circular economy, hand in hand with digitalisation.
